title: Proposition 39: Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.

context.text: Placed on the ballot by petition signatures (citizen initiative), per the Official Voter Information Guide.

question.text: PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT. Prohibits voting by mail unless voter designates a government-issued identification number for their voter registration. Invalidates mail ballots if envelope does not include last four digits of a government-issued identification number matching the number designated in the voter's registration (e.g., if voter designates Social Security number for registration, but provides driver's license number on envelope, their ballot would not count). Prohibits voting in person without presenting government-issued identification. Requires elections officials to annually report percentage of each county's voters whose citizenship status they have verified.

summary.text: Requires state and local elections officials to make "best efforts" using government data to verify that registered voters are U.S. citizens and to report annually the share of each county's voters verified. Voters must select a government-issued ID in their registration to vote by mail; in-person voters must present government-issued ID; mail voters must write the last four digits of the selected ID on the ballot envelope, to be matched to registration. The state would issue a free voter ID card on request, the State Auditor would report every odd-numbered year on compliance, and the Legislature would need to pass laws defining details such as acceptable IDs. Fiscal impact per the Legislative Analyst: state and local costs of tens of millions to low hundreds of millions of dollars each year, depending on future decisions, with possible smaller savings from fewer registered voters.

measure.yesMeans: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
measure.noMeans: A voter's identity would continue to be established with the voter's signature.

argumentsFor.text: Official argument in favor, signed by Margit Whitlock, Tafa Jefferson and Joe Green (Democratic, Republican and Independent Coalition Chairs, Californians for Voter ID): "Prop. 39 keeps mail ballots, extended polling hours and all other conveniences in place for voting accessibility," and "even guarantees every voter a FREE Voter ID if they want one."
Same argument: "In the last election, more than 100,000 ballots were rejected due to signature mismatches—and more than 200,000 voters endured hassles just to get their vote to count."

argumentsAgainst.text: Official argument against, signed by David Trujillo (ACLU California Action), Darius Kemp (Common Cause) and Lorrel Plimier (League of Women Voters of California): "voters would have to include a personal ID number on their ballot envelope that has to exactly match state records. Get one digit wrong, and a valid ballot could get thrown out."

Same argument: "'Free' state IDs aren't free: voters still pay for transportation, time off work, and costs like childcare or getting required documents," and "Prop. 39 will make every vote by mail voter include their personal details on their return envelope—making voters easy targets for identity theft."
